title: GET /api/v1/clusters/{cluster}/waf/findings: result
description: What the WAF found per object and rule over the last days, still needing a decision. A finding quotes what the engine matched in a request, so it can hold a visitor's input.

days.description: Value. How many days back the findings reach.

truncated.description: Value. True where the week held more findings than are given: the newest are, the older ones are not.

objects.description: The objects with findings, by name.

mode.description: Code. What the WAF does on a match: log it or block the request.

requests_judged.description: Value. How many requests the WAF judged for the object in the period.

clients.description: Value. How many clients made them.

findings.description: The findings, one per rule and field.

rule.description: Value. The rule set's number for the rule; stable, and the number an exception names.

kind.description: Text. The page's name for the kind of attack the rule's file covers, such as SQL injection. Match on rule instead.

explanation.description: Text. The page's sentence on that kind.

message.description: Text. The rule set's own message for the rule.

severity.description: Code. The rule set's severity for the rule; empty where the installed rule set does not define it.

field.description: Value. The part of the request the rule matched, in the engine's name for it, such as ARGS:q; empty where the rule names none.

field_label.description: Text. The same part as a person names it, such as q.

matched.description: Value. What the engine matched, as the visitor sent it; may be empty.

paths.description: Value. Paths the finding was made on, the most frequent first.

more_paths.description: Value. How many more paths there were than are listed.

clients.description: Value. How many clients made them.

last_seen.description: Value. When a request last matched.

in_draft.description: Value. True where an exception in the object's unpublished draft already covers the finding.

not_working.description: Value. True where a published exception covers the finding and it is still matched after the exception reached the nodes.
